ImageDescription.value:
1909 Ford Model T Touring Car, with its hood removed, at Waurn Ponds near Geelong, Victoria, Australia. (1909 Model T Touring Car models were originally painted either red or dark green, not black like this one.)

(Original source description:)

The Ford Motor Company was established in 1903, The Model T Ford was built from 1908-1927, a few models were built before the Model T, but the T was the first mass produced car. Ford wanted to keep the price low as possible, so to increase efficiency, he was the first to use assembly line production. Ford also made use of the knock-down kit concept, so almost from the beginning, the Model T was built in many other countries as well as the US, such as England and Australia.

The first car imported to Australia was the Model A in 1904, The Model T imported from 1909. From 1925, Fords were assembled in Geelong, Australia. This car is one of the first Model Ts imported.

The Model T slowly developed over its production life;

1909-14 T1; Flat top hood, flat cowl below the screen and gas lights. Cars from 1913 to 14 had the dog leg windscreen

1915-16 T2; had louvres in hood, contoured cowl and electric lights..

1917-23 T3; The hood tapered with a curved top, hinges moved.

1923-25 T4; Angled Screen, taller and wider at firewall.

1926-27 T5; Wire wheels, cowl now similar to Model A.

Body styles available in 1909 were; 2 door sedan, 2 door coupe, the tourer, the towncar and the roadster.

Engine; 20hp 177 Cu in

46873180.title: File:1913 Ford Model T T1 Tourer (19830968119).jpg

ImageDescription.value:
Ford Model T Touring Car. This car is unusual: it has a "1913" badge, but at first glance it is of 1915–1916 style, especially the flared "cowl" behind the hood and the straight windshield without support rods. Other features, such as the hood without louvres and the straight rear fenders, are of pre-1915 type, and the doors are 1913-style. The gas headlamps could be either vintage, since such headlamps were still in use on some early 1915 cars. The wire-spoked wheels are custom.

Конвейерная линия Генри Форда (фото 1913 года).

The Ford Motor assembly plant in La Boca, Buenos Aires. Opened in 1922, this was the first plant of the U.S. company in Argentina after arriving to the country in 1913.
The production line then moved to Gral. Pacheco in Greater Buenos Aires in 1962, where it still stands (a closer look at the cars shows their radiators are 1924-25 style, with the apron at the bottom of the shell).
The facility, located on Wenceslao Villafañe 40, is today property of Víctor Contreras S.A., a tubing and storage tank manufacturer.
